title: Arabidopsis accessions and their difference in heat tolerance during meiosis
content: With the changing climate, it is becoming more and more crucial to understand the natural existing heat tolerance in plants for agricultural and breeding purposes. The model plant Arabidopsis thaliana is well suited for the study of natural genetic variation with its many sequenced accessions (Lian et al. 2024). In this issue of Plant Physiology, Zhao and colleagues analyzed and compared 2 of those accessions, Columbia (Col-0) and Landsberg erecta (Ler), and their hybrids to understand the mechanisms behind meiotic heat tolerance (Zhao et al. 2024).
